XMLDB.COMMENT: XMLDB file for the AI Router routing rules

TABLE.NAME: aiprovider_router_rule
TABLE.COMMENT: Routing rules, evaluated in sortorder and then id order until one matches.

FIELD.NAME: name
FIELD.COMMENT: Administrator facing name. Never shown to end users.

FIELD.NAME: enabled
FIELD.COMMENT: Disabled rules are skipped without being deleted.

FIELD.NAME: sortorder
FIELD.COMMENT: Priority. Lowest is evaluated first, and is renumbered from zero on every write.

FIELD.NAME: targetid
FIELD.COMMENT: The ai_providers instance to delegate to. Deliberately not a foreign key, so that deleting a provider instance in core cannot fail.

FIELD.NAME: timestart
FIELD.COMMENT: Rule is not evaluated before this time. Zero means no start.

FIELD.NAME: timeend
FIELD.COMMENT: Rule is not evaluated after this time. Zero means no end.

TABLE.NAME: aiprovider_router_condition
TABLE.COMMENT: Conditions of a rule. All of them must be met, and each one is satisfied by any of the values it holds.

FIELD.NAME: type
FIELD.COMMENT: Condition type, such as course or promptlength. One of each type per rule at most.

FIELD.NAME: configdata
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON understood only by the condition type named above.

TABLE.NAME: aiprovider_router_log
TABLE.COMMENT: One row per AI request the router handled, including the ones it turned down.

FIELD.NAME: courseid
FIELD.COMMENT: Resolved the same way the rule engine resolves it. Null when the request came from outside any course.

FIELD.NAME: actionname
FIELD.COMMENT: The action basename, matching what core records, so the two logs can be compared.

FIELD.NAME: ruleid
FIELD.COMMENT: The rule that chose the target, if one did.

FIELD.NAME: rulename
FIELD.COMMENT: Copied because rules get renamed and deleted, and a log nobody can read is not a log.

FIELD.NAME: targetname
FIELD.COMMENT: Copied for the same reason as the rule name.

FIELD.NAME: targetprovider
FIELD.COMMENT: The component of the instance delegated to, which is what prices are looked up by.

FIELD.NAME: reason
FIELD.COMMENT: Why it failed, in terms an administrator can act on: declined, every target failed, a target threw.

FIELD.NAME: attempts
FIELD.COMMENT: How many targets were tried, so that the fallback chain can be seen working.

FIELD.NAME: cost
FIELD.COMMENT: Worked out when the row was written, never recalculated. Null when no price was known.

FIELD.NAME: keysource
FIELD.COMMENT: Who paid. Always site until BYOK arrives; the column exists now so that history does not have a hole in it.

TABLE.NAME: aiprovider_router_daily
TABLE.COMMENT: A day of the log, summarised, so that reports outlive the detail rows the purge removes. Deliberately holds no userid: a summary that named people would have to be rebuilt every time somebody exercised their right to be forgotten.

FIELD.NAME: daystart
FIELD.COMMENT: Midnight of the day summarised, in the server timezone. Not named day, because core already uses that name for a day of the month.

FIELD.NAME: courseid
FIELD.COMMENT: Null for requests made outside any course, exactly as in the log.

FIELD.NAME: targetid
FIELD.COMMENT: Null for requests that reached no target at all, which is how refusals and total failures are counted.

FIELD.NAME: targetname
FIELD.COMMENT: Carried over from the log for the same reason it is kept there: once the detail rows are purged this is the only readable name left.

FIELD.NAME: currency
FIELD.COMMENT: Grouped on, so that changing the site currency splits the summary instead of adding unlike figures together.

FIELD.NAME: cost
FIELD.COMMENT: The costs recorded at the time added up, never recalculated. Null when no request that day had a rate.

FIELD.NAME: costedrequests
FIELD.COMMENT: How many of the requests had a cost. Without it a total cannot be told apart from a total of the few requests a rate happened to cover.

FIELD.NAME: timecreated
FIELD.COMMENT: When the summary was written, which is not the day it describes.

TABLE.NAME: aiprovider_router_price
TABLE.COMMENT: What a provider charges, as the administrator has entered it, with the date each rate took effect.

FIELD.NAME: provider
FIELD.COMMENT: Provider component. Rates belong to a provider and a model, not to an instance, since two instances of the same provider are charged alike.

FIELD.NAME: model
FIELD.COMMENT: Empty means this rate covers any model of that provider which has no rate of its own. Declared without a default, because XMLDB refuses an empty string as one.

FIELD.NAME: promptrate
FIELD.COMMENT: Per million prompt tokens, in the site currency.

FIELD.NAME: completionrate
FIELD.COMMENT: Per million completion tokens.

FIELD.NAME: imagerate
FIELD.COMMENT: Per image, since image actions carry no token counts.

FIELD.NAME: timefrom
FIELD.COMMENT: When this rate took effect. A request is costed with the latest rate in force at the time.

TABLE.NAME: aiprovider_router_target
TABLE.COMMENT: Per delegation target settings for bring your own key. The name of the field a key goes in differs from provider to provider, so it is guessed and then confirmed by an administrator rather than assumed.

FIELD.NAME: targetid
FIELD.COMMENT: The ai_providers instance. Not a foreign key, so that deleting a provider instance in core cannot fail.

FIELD.NAME: keyfield
FIELD.COMMENT: Which of the instance config keys holds the key. Empty means the administrator has confirmed this provider takes no key at all, which is different from not having been asked yet. Declared without a default, because XMLDB refuses an empty string as one.

TABLE.NAME: aiprovider_router_key
TABLE.COMMENT: Keys brought by a user or registered for a course, encrypted with the site key. One key per subject and delegation target.

FIELD.NAME: scope
FIELD.COMMENT: Whose key it is: user or course.

FIELD.NAME: scopeid
FIELD.COMMENT: The user id or the course id, according to the scope.

FIELD.NAME: targetid
FIELD.COMMENT: The ai_providers instance this key is for. Keys belong to an instance rather than to a provider plugin, because two instances of one plugin can point at different endpoints.

FIELD.NAME: secret
FIELD.COMMENT: The key, encrypted with core\encryption. Never logged, never exported and never shown again.

FIELD.NAME: hint
FIELD.COMMENT: The last few characters, so that the owner can recognise which key this is without anything being decrypted. Deliberately the end of the key: the beginning is often a fixed prefix. Declared without a default, because XMLDB refuses an empty string as one.

FIELD.NAME: timeverified
FIELD.COMMENT: When the key was last tested against the provider. Zero means never.

FIELD.NAME: verifystatus
FIELD.COMMENT: What that test said.

FIELD.NAME: usermodified
FIELD.COMMENT: Who registered it. For a course key this is the only personal data in the row, and it is what a deletion request clears.
